messages:
jamie: Quick question ahead of tomorrow's handoff — can we align on SRE vs Runtime responsibilities and who we page for different failure classes? I'm writing the handoff note and want the wording to be clear. :thinking:

alexa: Short version: SRE owns infra (hosts, networking, cluster autoscaler, k8s control-plane, storage), Runtime owns model-serving (model binaries, inference server, model-specific config, quantization/kernels). If the failure is obviously in model inference (500 in model-server, KV cache corrupted, model mismatch) page Runtime first. If node-level (OOM, disk full, node NotReady, network partition) page SRE.

mike: A few gotchas we've hit: 1) high token latency from bad batching config looked like 'model slowness' but root cause was noisy neighbor/oversubscription -> SRE. 2) Bad model rollout causing corrupted state in cache -> Runtime. So when in doubt check `kubectl top` / node metrics quickly.

rachel: Proposed escalation path:
1) Pager to affected oncall (runtime or sre) depending on first-check classification.
2) If escalated and not acknowledged in 5m or wrong team, escalate to both leads @sam (runtime lead) and @alexa (sre lead).
3) Sev0/all-hands -> page @eng-sre and @eng-runtime leads and execs per playbook.

sam: Agree. Also add this pragmatic rule: if an API path returns 5xx but k8s shows node unhealthy -> SRE. If only process level restarts and pod logs show model errors -> Runtime.

oncall-bot: Reminder: handoff window starts in 30m. jamie -> mike. Add handoff note to #eng-oncall/handoffs.

jamie: I'll add a short decision tree to the handoff note. Draft:

``
If 1) host unhealthy (node NotReady, kernel panic, disk full) -> Page SRE oncall.
If 2) inference server returns 5xx or model is returning corrupted responses (bad tensors, repeated crashes on startup) -> Page Runtime oncall.
If 3) latency spikes but infra healthy -> check batching & KV cache -> Runtime unless CPU/GPU saturations visible.
If unsure -> page both (runtime+sre) and mark as Sev1 until diagnosis.
``

alexa: Tiny addition: include who to cc for customer-impacting lanes (prod traffic) — support-lead and customer-success.

mike: I'll pick up the 11:00 handoff. jamie I'll update the handoff doc and include the two examples above. :+1:

rachel: One more: define 'incident' for oncall notes — my suggestion:
- Incident = any event causing degraded service for customers (increased errors, >x latency, or loss of throughput) or risk of harm (data loss, security). Anything else is an operational alert that can be handled async.

jamie: Perfect. I'll add that definition and push the handoff doc link in 15m. Thanks all. :rocket:
